name: PT Multi Garam Utama Tbk

frontmatter.title: Multi Garam Utama: a data-centre story wrapped around a book-value holding
frontmatter.summary: FOLK trades at Rp59 after anchor supply and a weak tape. The 4 November Q3 release shows a IDR18.4bn nine-month profit that is a non-cash asset step-up, not operating cash; we now carry that step-up in the valuation and mark Traya at its run-rate rather than at cost. After a 30% holdco discount and capitalised overhead, the target is Rp27. We keep SELL; the return is -54.1%.
thesis: The market capitalises a data-centre platform; what FOLK actually owns is a water and wastewater treatment supplier with an undisclosed contract value [S6][S5].
The nine-month profit is an accounting result taken below EBIT: Q3 revenue was IDR5.1bn and the operating base has lost money at the EBITDA line in every year since listing [S0][S19].
The balance sheet is genuinely net cash, but after the fall the market value of IDR241.4bn still sits above Q3 group equity of IDR140.5bn [S0][S19].

Our sum of the parts — a residual book floor, DGNS at market, Traya at its annualised run-rate, the Q3 non-cash step-up, cash less capitalised holdco overhead — sits far below the share price even before the holdco discount [S0][S16][S19].
No dated catalyst exists to narrow the discount: no dividend, no buyback, no disclosed asset sale and no upstream cash, while the anchor holder is still selling [S2][S33][S10].

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited accounts — nine-month Traya consolidation and the first test of whether the reported profit converts to cash (statutory deadline, not a company-sourced date)
MSCI consultation feedback closes on Indonesia's proposed standalone status (market-wide)
MSCI final decision on Indonesia's index classification

blocks.text: **What changed and why.** This update carries the 4 November Q3 release and two mark changes into the model; it is not an explanation of the share-price move. The price evidence is thin and we do not overstate it. The last sourced level, in mid-October, was well above the current price; against Rp59 on 4 November the shares are down about a quarter [S2], and the exchange had already placed FOLK under unusual-market-activity surveillance in October [S4][S28]. On 3 November a Pasardana summary said Sumber Garam Pratama, a holder above five per cent, had sold 73.7 million shares and cut its stake to 18.4%; the article body could not be retrieved and the summary carries no transaction date or price, so we treat this as a post-hoc supply disclosure, not a value signal and not a proven cause of the fall [S33]. The one sale with a disclosed price remains the October block at 100.0 [S2]. Nothing in the operating record explains the move either: the Q3 release reports an attributable profit of IDR18.4bn for the nine months and a quarterly group profit of IDR20.4bn, but on Q3 revenue of only IDR5.1bn and struck below EBIT [S19][S20].

What the new release does change is the equity. Group assets rose to IDR152.0bn and group equity to IDR140.5bn at 30 September, and the Q3 group profit of IDR20.4bn equals that group asset and equity step-up almost exactly [S19][S20][S0]. That is a non-cash revaluation, not operating cash. We now carry the IDR18.4bn attributable step-up in the valuation bridge, and we mark Traya at its annualised Q3 revenue run-rate rather than at the nominal acquisition cost; both are sourced to the release and explained in the financial and valuation sections [S19]. We keep the SELL rating and move the target to Rp27; the return is -54.1% from Rp59 [S0].

FOLK is a small multi-sector holding that listed in 2023 as a media, retail-brand and intellectual-property group, then recapitalised through a private placement and pivoted into healthcare and infrastructure [S3][S10]. The share price ran from a few dozen rupiah to a four-digit high and has since fallen sharply, leaving a market capitalisation of IDR241.4bn against group equity of IDR140.5bn at 30 September 2026 [S0][S19].

The variant view is simple and uncomfortable: the data-centre exposure that the market is paying for is not a data-centre business. FOLK's infrastructure arm, Traya Hydro, supplies water and wastewater treatment to two large projects in the Cikarang cluster, and the company explicitly declines to disclose the contract value or the identity of the developers [S6]. The cluster itself is large, with announced investment above 6 billion and planned capacity above 600 MW, but those are the developers' numbers, not FOLK's order book [S6]. We still cannot find a contract value, margin or term for Traya in the public record; the only hard number is the revenue it has started to contribute, which we now use as a run-rate mark [S19].

What moves the value is therefore not a data-centre multiple but four observable things: the cash and the listed Diagnos stake, marked at the 27 October close; Traya's consolidated revenue run-rate; the residual book floor of the operating businesses, which is not an independent mark; and the Q3 non-cash step-up, less capitalised holdco overhead and the discount the market applies to the holding structure [S0][S16][S19]. The first is real but modest relative to the price; the second is now a mark rather than a cost placeholder; the third is a loss-making media and retail estate; the fourth is an accounting uplift whose composition is not disclosed. At Rp59 the shares still change hands above a post-discount SOTP of Rp24 per share [S0][S4]. A reader who wants the bull case should read the scenario section: it requires a disclosed contract with a sourceable value and a named corporate action, neither of which exists today.

FOLK describes itself as a multi-sector investment holding listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, rooted in new media, retail brands and intellectual property and now expanding into healthcare, mining and resources, and utility infrastructure [S10]. The legacy operating estate includes the digital media platform Folkative, the media and content assets USS Networks and Finfolk, the fashion brand Amazara, the hygiene brand Dr. Soap and the make-up brand Syca [S9][S14]. These are small consumer and media businesses, not a scaled platform; the group employed only 38 people at the last disclosure [S0]. The company describes its approach as active stewardship and disciplined capital allocation, but the operating footprint remains small, Jakarta-based and concentrated in a handful of brands [S10].

The strategy changed after the January 2026 private placement, which brought in roughly IDR54.0bn of share premium and took the share count to about four thousand million shares [S3]. Management then acquired 99.96 per cent of Traya Multi Investama for a nominal consideration, gaining control of Traya Hydro, a water technology company that provides integrated water and wastewater treatment through membrane filtration systems [S5][S12]. In May 2026 FOLK subscribed to new Diagnos shares in a private placement, taking a stake in the listed clinical-laboratory operator [S11][S13]. The company frames this as a shift from a creative-consumer ecosystem to a diversified investment platform [S3].

The group structure is a listed parent over unlisted operating subsidiaries plus a minority stake in a listed healthcare company. Traya Hydro is owned 99.9 per cent through the Traya Multi Investama vehicle, which FOLK acquired for IDR0.2bn [S5][S6]. Diagnos is listed under DGNS, and FOLK bought 95 million new shares at 269.0, a total investment of IDR25.6bn [S11]. Sumber Garam Pratama held 825 million shares after selling a block in October 2026, and a 3 November summary puts its stake at 18.4% after a further sale of 73.7 million shares [S2][S33]. The data pack's free-float and insider percentages are dated 4 November but reflect the register before that 3 November block; adjusted for it, the free float is nearer a third and the insider block lower, both still comfortably above the exchange minimum [S0][S17]. The filings we hold do not name a single controlling shareholder and do not rank holders, so we describe Sumber Garam Pratama only as a declared holder rather than assert control.

The ownership picture matters because the group's expansion has been funded by equity issued to new investors rather than by operating cash flow [S3]. The company's own investor-relations page lists annual reports, quarterly financial information and shareholder meetings, but the links currently resolve to a placeholder test document rather than to filed accounts, so a public investor cannot read the audited annual report from the company website [S10]. That is a transparency gap we treat as a governance flag, not a data inconvenience; it is also why the parent-only cost split and the Q2-Q3 non-operating items cannot be verified.

FOLK sits in the IDX-IC conglomerates bucket, but its economics are those of a tiny diversified holding rather than a scaled industrial group. The relevant sub-markets are Indonesian digital media and consumer brands, clinical diagnostics, and water and wastewater treatment for industrial and data-centre customers [S10][S12][S13]. Each is competitive and none is a natural monopoly. The media properties compete for audience and advertising with far larger platforms, the consumer brands compete on shelf space and online acquisition cost, and the water-treatment business competes for engineering, procurement and construction contracts against established plant suppliers.

The data-centre cluster is the only part of the story with visible external momentum. The Cikarang area has become Indonesia's largest data-centre development cluster, with developers announcing investment above 6 billion and combined capacity above 600 MW, and potential expansion toward a gigawatt [S6]. That is a genuine demand driver for water treatment, cooling and wastewater services. However, the value capture depends on contract terms, pricing and the ability to execute multiple projects simultaneously, and FOLK discloses none of these for Traya [S6].

Regulation and market structure are two-sided. On the one hand, Indonesia's digital and healthcare demand is growing with GDP, and the macro deck has real GDP growth of 5.3 per cent for FY2027E, which supports advertising, diagnostics and infrastructure spending [S0]. On the other hand, the exchange is removing high-shareholding-concentration names from the IHSG calculation from 2 November 2026 [S17], and MSCI opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone, with feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027 [S18]. FOLK itself is not on the published HSC list and its free float, on the register before the November block, is 31.3%, comfortably above the exchange minimum [S0][S17], so the direct index risk is market-wide rather than name-specific; it still reduces the passive bid for small, concentrated holdings.

The moat assessment is weak. Traya Hydro's membrane technology is differentiated at the project level but not proprietary in a way that protects pricing; the media brands have audience relationships but no durable pricing power; and the healthcare stake is a minority position with no control [S11][S12][S13]. Five-forces pressure is high from suppliers of membrane equipment and from rival engineering firms, high from buyers who can multi-source water treatment, moderate from new entrants in media, and low from substitutes in diagnostics. The one structural advantage is the parent's net cash, which lets it bid for small projects without balance-sheet stress [S3]. In water treatment specifically, the customer relationship is project-based and lumpy, so a single large contract can flatter one year of revenue without creating recurring earnings [S6][S12].

For a holding company, the industry question is less about any single segment and more about whether the centre allocates capital well. The record so far is a sequence of small related-party and negotiated transactions rather than a demonstrated ability to buy assets cheaply and upstream cash [S5][S11][S10]. We therefore treat the conglomerate structure as a discount factor, consistent with the house holdco method, rather than as a source of synergy value.

The reported history is one of shrinkage and losses. Revenue fell from IDR40.2bn in FY2022 to IDR24.8bn, IDR19.4bn and IDR18.8bn in the following years, while gross profit recovered only because the low-margin retail business was wound down [S0]. Operating costs did not shrink with the top line: SG&A was IDR23.4bn against gross profit of IDR9.8bn, producing an EBIT loss of IDR-13.6bn and an EBITDA loss of IDR-9.6bn [S0]. The company reports that operating expenses changed -22.4% in 2025, which is directionally helpful but not enough to close the gap at the current revenue base [S3].

The first three quarters of 2026 are dominated by non-operating items rather than by an operating turnaround. FOLK reported a net profit of IDR14.8bn in Q1 2026, its first profit since listing, but the operating line was still negative and the profit came from below EBIT [S0][S3]. In Q2 2026 the sign reversed: the company reported a net loss while operating EBIT remained negative, and the swing below EBIT accounted for essentially all of it [S0]. In Q3 the sign reversed again: the company reports IDR20.4bn of group net profit on IDR5.1bn of revenue, taking the nine-month attributable profit to IDR18.4bn and nine-month basic EPS to 4.5 [S19][S20]. Note that the quarterly figure is group net profit, while the nine-month figure is the portion attributable to the parent, because minorities carried a small loss [S20].

The Q3 composition can now be bounded, even though it is not fully disclosed. Group assets rose from the June balance sheet to IDR152.0bn and group equity to IDR140.5bn at 30 September, so the group equity increase and the Q3 group profit are almost the same number [S19][S20][S0]. The profit is therefore an asset step-up, not operating cash. A Diagnos mark-up is arithmetically excluded: the stake is 95 million shares and the May placement price was 269.0 against a 288.0 close, so the whole mark-up is far smaller than the gain [S11][S16]. A Traya bargain-purchase gain would have been struck at the April 2026 acquisition date, in Q2, not in Q3 [S5][S19]. The most likely location is therefore a fair-value revaluation or a reversal of the Q2 below-EBIT charge in the residual estate. We carry the IDR18.4bn attributable amount in the valuation bridge at its face value, because total equity is the same whether the accountants booked it to the residual or to Traya; what is not known is whether the revaluation will repeat or reverse, and that is why the P&L is not the valuation. No Q2 or Q3 2026 LK is archived and the IR site serves a placeholder, so this remains an evidence gap rather than a full reconciliation [S10].

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the company. The January placement added IDR54.0bn of share premium, total equity rose to IDR137.8bn by March 2026, total assets reached IDR147.5bn, and liabilities were only IDR9.7bn with no bank debt [S3]. By the September 2026 release equity had risen to IDR140.5bn and total assets to IDR152.0bn, still with no bank debt [S19]. The last full balance sheet we hold is June's, which shows no debt and a substantial cash balance, so net debt is negative [S0]. The Q3 release does not disclose cash, so the Q3 cash bound is the June balance plus or minus the quarter's operating cash flow, or plus any disposal proceeds. We found no disclosure of an asset sale after the balance-sheet date, which is not the same as proof that none occurred; a disposal would put post-sale cash above the June level [S19][S2][S33]. That net cash is real and is the main reason we do not value the equity at zero. It is also why the market's valuation is still difficult to justify: a net-cash holding with a loss-making operating estate trades at IDR241.4bn, above its own reported equity [S0][S19].

Our forecast holds the operating run-rate rather than assuming a rescue. Revenue grows 2% in FY2026E and 5% a year thereafter, gross margin stays near 52%, and SG&A is held at 100% of revenue, a rounded-up hold above the Q2 2026 observed ratio that the data pack's own line items imply [S0], not that observed ratio itself. D&A is held at the FY2025 actual 21% of revenue rather than the lower FY2024 ratio, so the EBIT line is not flattered by a falling charge [S0]. On those assumptions EBITDA remains negative through the forecast, at IDR-5.2bn in FY2026E. This is an operating-basis forecast: revenue, gross margin, SG&A, D&A and tax only, with every below-EBIT item set to zero, so its negative parent net profit is not an as-reported year and does not contradict the IDR18.4bn nine-month attributable profit the company has already printed [S19][S20]. The forecast balance sheet is an operating roll only: it does not capitalise the January placement proceeds, which are already inside the June actual cash of the valuation, so its equity and net-debt lines are not a forecast of the reported balance sheet and we do not use a forecast-book multiple anywhere in this report. The valuation rests on the June 2026 cash balance, the Q3 step-up in the bridge and the marks below; the Q3 release confirms the equity but not its cash composition [S0][S19].

Earnings quality is poor on several measures. The accruals picture is distorted by negative working capital and by the retail wind-down, and cash flow from operations was negative in FY2025, so reported losses are not being flattered by working-capital releases [S0]. The larger flag is that all of the reported profit is struck below EBIT and is non-cash: Q3 alone contributed IDR20.4bn against revenue of IDR5.1bn, the nine-month attributable figure is IDR18.4bn, and the balance-sheet step-up is the same order of magnitude [S19][S20]. That is an accruals-class flag, not a cash-generation story: the profit is larger than the revenue that produced it, so it cannot be a margin on operations, and the release does not disclose what was revalued. We carry the step-up in the bridge because it is reported equity, not because we can verify it, and we do not treat it as recurring. Related-party gravity is present: the Traya acquisition was a nominal transaction with the controlling director retaining a residual share, and the group's expansion is being executed through negotiated transactions rather than open tenders [S5][S10]. We classify these as optics-class and structure flags, not as evidence of fabricated cash, but they are why the residual book floor is labelled a floor and why the Q3 uplift is shown separately rather than folded into it.

Capital allocation has been equity-funded and acquisition-led. The company raised fresh equity, bought a nominal stake in Traya, subscribed to a Diagnos placement and is now funding working capital for water-treatment projects [S3][S11][S6]. It has never paid a dividend, and the payout assumption is therefore zero [S0]. Until the operating businesses generate free cash flow, the holding depends on the placement proceeds and on the controlling shareholder's willingness to keep supporting it, which is a weaker form of financial flexibility than internally generated cash.

We value FOLK on a sum of the parts because the company is a holding with no single homogeneous earnings stream and because its listed stake, its unlisted operating estate and its cash can each be identified [S0][S16]. The house method for conglomerates is SOTP with honest marks: listed stakes at market value, unlisted segments at book or a sourced metric, less holdco net debt, less holdco overhead capitalised at about ten times, less a holding-company discount anchored to the base rate [S0]. We do not use P/E because the trailing profit is a below-EBIT accounting result and forecast parent earnings are negative, and we do not use the own-history P/BV multiple because the FY2025 observation is contaminated by the squeeze to a four-digit share price [S0][S19].

The parts are as follows. The Diagnos stake is marked at market, not cost: 95 million shares at the 27 October 2026 close of 288.0 [S16][S11], which is above the IDR25.6bn FOLK paid in May [S11]. Traya Hydro is no longer marked at its nominal acquisition cost of IDR0.2bn: the Q3 release attributes the whole revenue increase to the Traya water-filter segment, and Q3 revenue of IDR5.1bn grew 36.7% year on year [S19]. On the prior-year base that is roughly a third more revenue in the quarter, so the annualised incremental run-rate is in the mid-single-digit billions of rupiah. We mark Traya at one times that annualised run-rate, the low end of the one-times-revenue to ten-times-fifteen-per-cent-margin cross-check, which is several times the acquisition cost and still a small fraction of NAV [S19][S5]. No contract value or term exists to justify a higher mark. The media, retail-brand and IP estate has no independent mark. The IDR18.8bn revenue base is loss-making at EBITDA, and the only sourceable figure is the residual of 30 June 2026 parent equity after cash, the Diagnos stake and Traya [S0]. We therefore carry it as a residual book floor, not a mark; it embeds every other asset and liability, so it is an upper bound on what a buyer would pay, not a valuation.

The Q3 step-up is carried as a separate bridge item rather than folded into the residual, at the IDR18.4bn attributable amount reported for the nine months [S19]. The reasoning is set out in the financial section: the step-up equals the group asset and equity increase, a Diagnos mark-up is arithmetically too small, and a Traya bargain-purchase gain would have been struck in Q2 at the April acquisition. The most likely location is therefore the residual estate. If the accountants instead booked it to Traya, the Traya carrying value would rise toward the same amount and our separate run-rate mark would be subsumed by it rather than added on top; the bridge is the neutral way to carry the gain until the LK says which asset moved. What we cannot do is mark it down without evidence: the June book is the last actual balance sheet, and carrying the reported September equity while refusing to recognise the increase in a buy case was the asymmetry the previous draft carried [S19][S20][S0].

The cost of equity is 11.9% and the WACC is 11.9%, reflecting a 0.90 levered beta, the mature-market risk-free rate and the Indonesia country premium in the house build [S0]. Because the company has no debt, the WACC equals the cost of equity and the discount rate is not the source of the valuation gap. The gap comes from the asset marks and from the holdco discount.

The bridge starts from the three gross parts, adds the Q3 non-cash step-up and the June 2026 net cash, and deducts capitalised holdco overhead. The overhead line is a minimum estimate, not a floor: no parent-only cost line is published, so we deduct about ten times an annual corporate overhead equal to roughly a tenth of the annualised Q2 SG&A, because the subsidiaries' costs are already inside the book floor and capitalising the whole consolidated SG&A would double-count them [S0]. It is the optimistic end of the range. A peer-like carry of about twice that amount, closer to the DSSA corporate-cost ratio, would reduce the target by roughly an eighth. This is an irreducible evidence gap — the IR site serves a placeholder and no audited LK is retrievable — and it is disclosed rather than hidden [S10].

We apply a holdco discount at the mid-point of the house base-rate range, because FOLK has net cash and no debt but also no dividend, a concentrated register, a related-party acquisition record, no dated catalyst to narrow the discount and a holder above five per cent that is still selling down [S2][S10][S33]. FOLK is not on the published HSC list, so HSC exclusion is not a factor in the discount and the earlier draft was wrong to cite it [S17]. The discount is applied to the whole SOTP in the engine, including net cash. That is the convention, not a claim that cash deserves a holdco discount: if cash were added undiscounted and only the operating parts discounted, the value would be about a seventh higher, which is a cross-check we state rather than adopt because the marks themselves are the larger uncertainty [S0]. That produces an asset value of Rp24 per share. The published target of Rp27 is that value rolled forward one year at the cost of equity, which is the engine's standard twelve-month convention. We state both: the convention adds about an eighth to an asset base whose own FY2026E ROE is negative and whose cash yields far less than the cost of equity, so the roll-forward flatters rather than understates [S0]. The target is not a liquidation value: it assumes the operating estate is worth its residual book floor, Traya is worth its run-rate and the Diagnos stake is worth its market price. Even on those marks the equity is worth a fraction of the current price.

The sensitivity table shows the target across holdco-discount and cost-of-equity steps. The discount dominates: a ten-percentage-point change in the discount moves the value by roughly a tenth of the gross asset base, while a fifty-basis-point change in the cost of equity barely moves it, because the SOTP is an asset valuation rather than a discounted earnings stream [S0]. The engine's reverse DCF cannot bracket today's price: no discount inside the plausible range, nor its complement, brings the pre-discount SOTP up to the market capitalisation, so the implied value is an out-of-range extrapolation rather than a solved discount.

We therefore state the gap attribution as an assumption rather than a measurement. Even after the fall to Rp59, the market capitalisation of IDR241.4bn is above the pre-discount net asset value of these marks, before the 30% holdco discount is applied [S0]. Under (a), the residual estate is at book and every other part is marked, so the whole pre-discount gap is an implied Traya option. Capitalising a water-treatment contractor at ten times earnings on a fifteen per cent net margin, that option implies contract revenue several times the group's entire IDR18.8bn FY2025 revenue, before execution, financing or the confidentiality the company imposes [S6]. Under (b), the residual is marked at one times its own revenue rather than at book; pre-discount NAV falls by the difference and the implied Traya option rises by the same amount. The variant depends on (a): if the market is instead paying above book for the media and IP estate, the implied Traya option falls. We use (a) because the residual has no independent mark and a loss-making estate does not obviously deserve one times revenue. That is the testable version of the variant view: on the most favourable defensible marks, the market is still not paying for the business FOLK owns; it is prepaying a contract FOLK has not disclosed.

We cross-check the SOTP against the market's own marks. The market capitalisation of IDR241.4bn is above reported group equity of IDR140.5bn at 30 September 2026, so the shares still trade at a premium to book after the fall [S0][S19]. We deliberately do not use a forecast-book multiple: the engine prints one, but it is struck on a forecast balance sheet that does not capitalise the January placement and is therefore not comparable to the reported accounts. The trailing P/E is not usable because the last twelve months' parent earnings are still negative after the Q2 charge, even though the nine-month 2026 figure is positive; the absence of a clean earnings multiple is itself informative, because a company that cannot be valued on a normalised earnings stream must be valued on assets, and its assets do not support the price [S0][S19].

The downside risks are governance, disclosure and liquidity, in that order. The anchor shareholder sold a block in October 2026 at a price well above the current market, and a 3 November summary says it sold a further 73.7 million shares, leaving 18.4% [S2][S33]. We treat the November item as supply, not as a signal about the holder's view of value: the summary gives no transaction date or price, and a forced or at-market block is a liquidity event rather than a valuation judgement [S33]. The stock was placed on the exchange's unusual-market-activity watchlist after a sharp move, which raises the risk of trading restrictions and of a regulatory request for explanation [S4]. The free float on the register before the November block is 31.3%, comfortably above the exchange minimum and not a name-specific index risk [S0][S17]; the index risk that matters is the market-wide MSCI consultation [S18]. The stock is also outside the fund's minimum-size universe: market capitalisation is IDR241.4bn, below the house floor, while average daily traded value of IDR6.2bn and the main-board listing pass [S0]. The position would have to be sized accordingly.

Macro risk is moderate. A weaker rupiah and higher domestic rates would raise the discount rate and reduce the value of the unlisted estate, while a stronger dollar would help the data-centre investment case at the margin by making the cluster more attractive to international developers [S0]. Commodity and currency exposure is indirect: FOLK does not produce commodities, but its water-treatment projects are priced in rupiah while some equipment is imported, so a weaker currency squeezes project margins. Operational risk is concentrated in Traya's ability to execute multiple projects with a small balance sheet and no disclosed contract terms [S6].

Liquidity is a separate constraint. Average daily traded value is IDR6.2bn, which is adequate for a small position but thin relative to the market capitalisation, and the unusual-market-activity notice shows how quickly the tape can become disorderly [S0][S4]. For a fund, the exit is the risk, not only the valuation.

The bear case assumes the data-centre story stays unquantified, the Q3 accounting profit does not repeat, the anchor keeps selling and the discount widens to the top of the house range. The base case assumes the residual book floor holds, the Q3 step-up is real equity, the Diagnos stake stays at market and the discount stays at the mid-point. The operating estate burns cash, which is real, and the June balance sheet carries the placement proceeds; the forecast cash line is an operating roll that excludes those proceeds, so we do not use it as a liquidity forecast. The bull case assumes a disclosed water-treatment contract with a sourceable value and a discount at the bottom of the range; because no value is disclosed, the contract is an option we describe rather than book. Probabilities are 25% bear, 50% base and 25% bull, with a mirrored discount shock in the engine [S0].

The engine's scenario shocks move model inputs, and the SOTP marks are fixed rows, so the table's bear widens the discount but cannot write the residual or the Diagnos stake down. The true downside cases are therefore shown as a memo, not as a fourth scenario. A halving of the residual book floor removes about three tenths of pre-discount NAV and, on the wide-end discount, takes the twelve-month target into the high teens. A full write-down removes about three fifths of pre-discount NAV and takes the target to roughly a sixth of today's price. A thirty per cent fall in the Diagnos mark removes about a seventeenth of NAV and cuts the target by about the same fraction; a fifty per cent fall removes about a tenth and cuts it by roughly a tenth. The stated bear is the top of the discount range on the marks we can defend, not the worst case; the book-stress bear is below it, and that is the asymmetry the previous draft carried [S0][S16][S19].

One further risk is that the holding structure itself becomes the story. If management uses the post-placement balance sheet for further negotiated acquisitions in healthcare or infrastructure, the discount should widen rather than narrow, because each transaction adds a new related-party mark that minority holders cannot independently value [S5][S11]. The reverse is also possible: a clean, arm's-length purchase of a cash-generating asset at a disclosed price would be the first evidence that the centre can allocate capital well, and we would raise the marks accordingly [S10].

The signposts that would change our view are specific. A contract announcement with a value, term and counterparty for Traya Hydro would move the infrastructure asset from a run-rate mark to a cash-flow mark; we would need the contract value and margin to underwrite it [S6]. A dividend or a buyback at the holdco level would be evidence that cash can be upstreamed; today there is none [S10]. A sale of the Diagnos stake at a premium to its 27 October market price would validate the listed mark [S16]. Conversely, a further related-party acquisition, a new share issue or a fresh block sale would widen the discount and validate the bear case [S2].

Ownership is concentrated. The data pack shows insiders holding 68.1% of the register and a free float of 31.3%, but those figures are dated 4 November and reflect the register before the 3 November block; adjusted for the 73.7 million shares sold, the free float is nearer a third and Sumber Garam Pratama's reported stake is 18.4% [S0][S2][S33]. The filings we hold do not name a single controlling shareholder, so we do not assert one. FOLK is not on the published high-shareholding-concentration list, so HSC exclusion is not a governance or discount factor for this name [S17]; its free float is above the exchange minimum [S0]; the exchange is removing HSC names from the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S17], and MSCI's standalone consultation is market-wide [S18]. None of that is a finding of wrongdoing, but concentration, the related-party record and the disclosure gap change the investor base and the liquidity profile.

Related-party dealings are a live issue. The Traya Multi Investama acquisition left the president director with a residual single share of the target, and the group's expansion into healthcare and infrastructure has been executed through negotiated transactions rather than open tenders [S5][S10]. The company's investor-relations page lists annual reports and quarterly information but currently serves a placeholder document, so the audited accounts are not readily available from the company website [S10]. We could not verify the auditor, the audit opinion, the board committees, the parent-only cost split or the Q2-Q3 2026 non-operating items from a company filing in this window. Those are irreducible evidence gaps, stated as gaps rather than papered over with an assumed number.

The dividend record is empty: no dividend has been paid since the 2023 listing, and the payout assumption is zero [S0]. The board is young and small, with a president director whose background is in venture capital and financial services and commissioners drawn from property and consumer businesses [S10]. We see no evidence of pledged controlling shares in the public record we reviewed, but the absence of a filing-level disclosure means we cannot rule it out.

ESG exposure is modest at the group level but specific at the asset level. The water-treatment business has a positive environmental rationale because it improves industrial water reuse and wastewater quality, and the data-centre cluster's water demand is a genuine sustainability issue [S6][S12]. The media and consumer brands have limited direct environmental footprint. The main social and governance issues are disclosure quality, related-party transacting and the concentration of ownership. Those are the factors we weigh inside the holdco-discount range; net cash and the absence of debt offset them, so we apply the mid-point rather than the wide end, and the residual book floor we carry is the generous side of the asset marks [S2][S10].

Q3 2026 has now printed: revenue of IDR5.1bn and nine-month attributable profit of IDR18.4bn, with Traya consolidated from April 2026 [S19][S20]. The release still discloses no contract value, margin or backlog for Traya, so the infrastructure asset is marked on its revenue run-rate, not on a contract [S6][S19]. The next dated checkpoint is the FY2026 audited accounts in the statutory window to 31 March 2027 — a nine-month Traya consolidation, because April is the first consolidated month, so FY2027 is the first full year — and it is the first test of whether the reported profit converts to cash. The deadline is general regulatory knowledge (the OJK annual-report rule), not a company-sourced date, and we do not cite the Q3 release for it. The MSCI consultation takes feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027, which will determine whether the passive bid for small Indonesian holdings improves or deteriorates [S18]. The exchange's removal of HSC names from the IHSG takes effect on 2 November 2026, but FOLK is not on the list, so it is a market-wide rather than a name-specific event [S17].

Between updates we monitor five KPIs: the cash balance and any drawdown of the placement proceeds [S3]; the EBITDA loss and whether SG&A stays near the Q2 2026 run-rate [S0]; the composition of the below-EBIT profit and whether it repeats [S19][S20]; any disclosed contract value or backlog at Traya Hydro [S6]; and the size and price of any further anchor-shareholder sales [S2][S33]. We also monitor the Diagnos stake at its 27 October market price against the IDR25.6bn cost, because a mark-to-market move changes the SOTP [S16][S11].

Holding companies in emerging markets often trade below the sum of their parts because minority shareholders cannot force the sale of assets or the upstreaming of cash. The discount tends to narrow only when a controller chooses to act, and it widens when related-party transactions or opaque disclosure raise the cost of trust. That is the framework we apply here rather than treating a low multiple as an automatic opportunity.

bear.narrative: The data-centre story stays unquantified, no contract value is disclosed, the Q3 accounting profit does not repeat, the >5% anchor keeps selling, and the market applies the wide end of the holdco range. The SOTP rows are fixed marks, so the engine's shock moves only the discount; the memo stress in section 5 halves and writes off the residual and marks DGNS down, and those are the true downside cases. A half write-down of the residual takes the target into the high teens; a full write-down takes it to about a sixth of today's price.

bull.narrative: DGNS is already marked at market in the base; the Q3 step-up is now carried in the bridge, Traya is marked at its annualised run-rate rather than at cost, and a disclosed water-treatment contract with a sourceable value would add an option the SOTP still does not carry. With the marks fixed, the only quantified engine lever is the discount narrowing to the bottom of the house range; the contract value the price implies is quantified in section 4, not booked here.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025 revenue was Rp18.8bn and H1-26 runs at about Rp19bn annualised; the media/retail/IP base is mature while Traya Multi Investama consolidates from April 2026, but no contract values are disclosed, so growth is held near nominal GDP after a flat 2026 [S0][S6].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross margin was 52% and H1-26 about 51%; held at 52% as water treatment and healthcare services enter the mix [S0][S6].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A was 125% of revenue; the Q2-26 ratio is 95.7% (5.037/5.262) per the data pack, and the 22.4% FY2025 opex cut is the company's own disclosure [S0][S3]. The base case holds opex at revenue and EBIT stays negative through the forecast [S0].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual ratio of 21% of revenue (Rp3.93bn on Rp18.76bn), the last audited year, rather than the lower FY2024 ratio [S0]. A higher D&A charge lowers EBIT and leaves EBITDA unchanged; group D&A was not restated in the pack because the LK notes could not be retrieved.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 0.6% and FY2024 1.3% of revenue; the media estate is capital-light and 2% covers maintenance plus small water-treatment equipment [S0][S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was negative at 12% of revenue after the retail wind-down; held near zero [S0].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The group is loss-making and the LK shows only minor tax credits, so no cash tax is modelled [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FOLK had no bank debt at Q1-26 and the Q2-26 pack shows zero debt [S3][S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Cash of about Rp45bn is held on deposit; 5.5% approximates the IDR time-deposit rate in the macro deck [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No debt and no funded expansion plan disclosed, so net borrowing is zero [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero: the model is an OPERATING-BASIS forecast (revenue, gross margin, SG&A, D&A, tax only) and deliberately excludes every below-EBIT item. The company has already reported 9M attributable profit of Rp18.40bn, which the report shows as reported; it is not an FY2026E forecast [S19][S20][S0].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities absorbed 27% of the FY2025 loss (a negative minority balance), so 27% is carried forward [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid since the 2023 listing and the company is investing its placement proceeds, so payout stays at zero [S0][S10].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose to 4,091mn after the January 2026 placement (3,948mn at FY2025), a 3.6% increase; no further issue is approved [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for IDR, below the 5.29% FY2027E real GDP path in the macro deck [S0].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: House base rate for holdco discounts is 20-40%; FOLK sits at the mid-point because it has net cash and no debt, offset by no dividend, a concentrated register, related-party acquisitions, no dated narrowing catalyst and a >5% anchor that is still selling down [S2][S10][S33]. FOLK is NOT on the published HSC list and that is not a discount-widening factor [S17]. The discount is applied to the whole SOTP in the engine, including net cash; a cash-undiscounted cross-check is shown in the report.

challenges.challenge: The update's trigger is not verifiable as stated. The "five-day share-price fall" to Rp59 [S0] has no fact for the five-day move: S23 carries only the IDX -7.52% weekly figure and does not mention FOLK, and the report gives no FOLK percentage. The second "fact behind it" is a 3 November Pasardana headline archived only as a Bing RSS snippet [S33]; it carries no transaction date or price. The report then calls that sale "a signal about the holder's own view of value" (section 5). A forced or at-market block is supply, not a value signal, and the price is unknown; the only sale with a price is the 25mn block at Rp100 on 14 Oct [S2].
challenges.answer: The Pasardana article body could not be archived (the page is script-rendered and the fetch returned no readable text), so there is still no transaction date or price. We now describe the 73.65mn-share item as a post-hoc supply disclosure with unknown price and date, drop the "holder's view of value" inference, and state the move from the S0 monthly close at end-October to Rp59 on 4 November instead of asserting a five-day fall. The only priced sale remains the 25mn block at Rp100 [S2]. S33 remains thin and is labelled so.

challenges.challenge: The Q3 composition is not wholly open. The 4 November release gives total assets of Rp151.99bn against Rp131.22bn at 30 June [S19][S0] and group equity of Rp140.46bn against Rp120.12bn (parent Rp136.00bn less minorities Rp-15.88bn), so the Q3 group profit of Rp20.35bn [S20] equals the balance-sheet increase almost exactly (assets +Rp20.77bn, equity +Rp20.34bn). The profit is therefore an asset step-up, not operating cash, and can only be a fair-value gain in the residual estate, a reversal of the Q2 -Rp15.6bn charge, or a gain on Traya (a bargain-purchase gain would put Traya's fair value near Rp20bn, not the Rp0.25bn cost). A DGNS mark-up is arithmetically excluded: 95.35mn x (288-269) = Rp1.81bn. The report holds cash at June Rp45.36bn and post_bs_review asserts "no asset sale" after the balance-sheet date, although no Q3 LK or filing supports that negative; a disposal would mean post-sale cash above Rp45.36bn.
challenges.answer: Reconciles: the Q3 group profit of Rp20.35bn equals the group asset and equity step-up almost exactly; a DGNS mark-up is arithmetically excluded (about Rp1.81bn); a Traya bargain-purchase gain would have been struck at the April acquisition in Q2, not Q3. We therefore allocate the Rp18.40bn attributable amount to the residual estate and carry it as a sourced valuation.bridge item, with Traya's own mark handled separately. The Q3 cash bound is stated as June cash plus or minus Q3 operating flow, or plus any disposal proceeds, and the text now says "no asset sale disclosed", not "no asset sale".

challenges.challenge: The bear never shocks the largest mark. The Rp64.74bn residual book floor is 55% of NAV (70% of gross parts) and the report itself calls it "an upper bound on what a buyer would pay" for a loss-making estate (FY2025 EBITDA -Rp9.6bn on Rp18.8bn revenue) [S0]. The bear only widens the discount to 40% (Rp19.3) and holds the residual at full book; the report calls a media write-down "the unmodelled tail" but never quantifies it. A 50% write-down gives ~Rp16.4 and a full write-down ~Rp10.2, both below the stated bear, so the current bear is a discount-widening case, not a downside case.
challenges.answer: The engine cannot shock a fixed SOTP row, so we say so explicitly and add the stress as a memo in section 5: halving the residual removes about three tenths of pre-discount NAV and takes the target into the high teens on the wide-end discount; a full write-down removes about three fifths and takes it to roughly a sixth of the current price. The table bear is now labelled a discount-widening case, not the true downside case, and the bear narrative points to the memo.

challenges.challenge: Traya is carried at its Rp0.2499bn related-party acquisition cost (0.2% of NAV) even though S19 shows Traya Group consolidated from April 2026 and attributes the whole Q3 revenue increase to the water-filter segment: Q3 revenue Rp5.09bn vs Rp3.73bn in Q3-25 (+36.7%) implies ~Rp1.36bn of incremental quarterly revenue, ~Rp5.5bn annualised [S19][S0]. A cross-check at 1x revenue or 10x a 15% margin puts Traya at Rp5-8bn, ~Rp1.0-1.5/share of target; the bargain-purchase hypothesis in section 3 would put it near Rp20bn, ~Rp4/share. The bull books neither, and its revenue +3pp shock is inert in an asset SOTP: bear Rp19.3 and bull Rp25.8 differ only by the +/-10pp discount.
challenges.answer: Traya is no longer at cost. The Q3 release attributes the whole revenue increase to the water-filter segment and gives the revenue growth rate [S19], which on the prior-year base implies a mid-single-digit-billion annualised incremental run-rate. We mark Traya at one times that run-rate (the low end of the one-times-revenue to ten-times-fifteen-per- cent-margin cross-check), which lifts the holding from Rp0.25bn to Rp5.5bn and the target with it. The revenue shock is removed from both scenarios because it is inert in an asset SOTP; the discount is the only quantified engine lever and the memo stresses carry the rest.

challenges.challenge: Two discount-base problems. (1) The 30% holdco discount is applied to the whole NAV including Rp25.36bn of net cash (Rp45.36bn cash less Rp20.0bn capitalised overhead): (92.45 + 25.36) x 0.7 = 82.47, or Rp20.16/share. Discounting cash removes Rp7.61bn, ~Rp1.86/share; discounting only the operating parts gives Rp22.02/share and a target of ~Rp24.6 (+9%). The house card does not say cash is discounted, and the peer mode (ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/DSSA 30%) does not settle it. (2) The holdco_discount basis cites "HSC exclusion" as a discount-widening factor, but sections 2/6 say FOLK is not on the published HSC list [S17] and the model registry has hsc.listed: false; the cited sources [S2][S4] [S10][S33] contain no HSC fact. The overhead deduction is also called a "floor" while it is the optimistic end: Rp2.0bn is only a tenth of consolidated Q2 SG&A (Rp20.1bn), and a DSSA-like Rp38.8bn carry would cut the target to ~Rp19.0.
challenges.answer: HSC exclusion is removed from the discount basis; we now cite S17 to say FOLK is NOT on the published HSC list and that HSC is not a factor. The report states that the 30% discount is applied to the whole SOTP including net cash (engine convention) and gives the cash-undiscounted cross-check, which is about a seventh higher than the stated value. The Rp20bn overhead is relabelled a minimum estimate, not a floor, and the text shows that a DSSA-like carry of about twice that would cut the target by roughly an eighth.

challenges.challenge: The treatment of the Q3 equity increase is asymmetric. The residual is struck on 30 June parent equity of Rp136.0bn and the report refuses to mark it up for the Rp18.40bn attributable Q3 profit because the composition is unknown, while the bear also refuses to mark it down. If the gain sits in the residual, adding it gives NAV of Rp136.21bn and a target of ~Rp26.1 (+16%); if it sits in Traya, the Traya mark should rise toward the same amount; only a DGNS mark-up would already be captured, and that is arithmetically excluded (Rp1.81bn). Either way the current Rp22.55 target carries a one-sided Rp18-20bn caution that the bull does not reverse.
challenges.answer: The Q3 attributable gain is now allocated to the residual estate and carried in valuation.bridge at Rp18.40bn with probability 1.0, sourced to the 4 November release. The target at the corrected mark is Rp27.1, up from Rp22.6; the base no longer holds the June book while refusing the increase. If the accountants booked the gain to Traya instead, the Traya carrying value would rise toward the same amount and the separate run-rate mark would be subsumed rather than added twice, which is why the bridge is the neutral treatment.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E model contradicts the 9M actual. The company has already reported 9M attributable profit of Rp18.40bn [S19][S20], but the model's FY2026E np_parent is -Rp6.65bn and section 3 states "net profit to parent remains negative [S0]". That implies a Q4 loss of ~Rp25.05bn, for which there is no source or explanation; the model excludes all non-operating items (other_nonop = 0), so it is an operating-basis number, not the as-reported year. Separately, D&A is set at 18% of revenue against 21% in FY2025 [S0], a downward drift that flatters EBIT by ~Rp0.6bn with no sourced reason.
challenges.answer: The forecast is now labelled explicitly as operating-basis: revenue, gross margin, SG&A, D&A and tax only, with other_nonop at zero, so its negative parent profit does not contradict the reported 9M Rp18.40bn, which the report shows separately as reported. D&A is reverted to the FY2025 actual 21% of revenue (Rp3.93bn/Rp18.76bn) rather than the lower FY2024 ratio, so EBIT is not flattered by a falling charge; EBITDA is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The only market mark in the SOTP is never stressed. DGNS is Rp27.46bn (30% of gross parts, 23% of NAV) at the 27 October close of Rp288 [S16]; it is a small, thinly traded listed stock and the SOTP holds it at market in both base and bear. A 30% DGNS fall cuts the target by ~Rp1.6 (to ~Rp21.0); a 50% fall to ~Rp144 gives ~Rp19.9, and 50% plus the 40% discount gives ~Rp17.1. The bear narrative says DGNS is "already marked at market", which is true but not a stress, and section 5 itself lists the DGNS mark as a monitorable driver.
challenges.answer: The stake is not exempt. Because the SOTP holds DGNS as a fixed row, the engine cannot shock it; section 5 now shows the mark-down as a memo: a 30% fall removes about a seventeenth of NAV and cuts the target by about the same fraction, a 50% fall removes about a tenth and cuts it by roughly a tenth. The earlier "already marked at market" language is retained only to explain why the base has no mark-up, not as a stress.

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF attributes the entire gap between the Rp241.4bn market cap and the Rp117.8bn pre-discount NAV to an implied Traya option, but the largest NAV component (Rp64.74bn, 55%) is a residual book floor that the report says is not a market mark. The gap could equally be the market valuing the media/IP estate above book, a control premium, or the Q3 gain; attributing it all to Traya overstates the implied contract (the "several times group revenue" conclusion) and weakens the variant's testability. If the residual were marked at 1x revenue (Rp18.8bn) rather than book, the implied Traya option would rise to ~Rp169bn; if the market is paying above book for the estate, it falls.
challenges.answer: The gap attribution is now stated as an assumption, not a measurement. Section 4 shows (a) residual at book: the whole pre-discount gap is an implied Traya option, which at ten times a fifteen-per-cent margin implies contract revenue several times group revenue; and (b) residual at one times its own revenue: pre-discount NAV falls by the difference and the implied Traya option rises by the same amount. The text makes clear the variant depends on (a) and that a market paying above book for the media/IP estate would reduce the implied option.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026 audit catalyst is unsourced and mislabelled. The frontmatter says "31 March 2027 - FY2026 audited accounts - first full year of Traya consolidation" and section 7 repeats "the first full year of Traya consolidation", both citing S19; S19 is the 4 November Q3 release, contains no audit date, and says Traya consolidated from April 2026 [S19], so FY2026 is a nine-month consolidation and FY2027 is the first full year. This repeats the prior round's L3/C11 sequencing correction in a new place, and fund record will track an unsourced date.
challenges.answer: Corrected. FY2026 is described as a nine-month Traya consolidation (April-December) and FY2027 as the first full year. The 31 March 2027 date is now stated as general regulatory knowledge (the OJK annual-report deadline), outside the source set, and S19 is no longer cited for the date or the sequencing; the frontmatter source field says so explicitly.

challenges.challenge: Register figures and prose are stale or overstated. Sections 2/6/7 use free float 31.31% and insiders 68.13% as of 4 November [S0], but the 3 November sale of 73.65mn shares (1.80% of 4,091mn) changes the register: free float is ~33.1%, and if SGP is counted inside the insider block, insiders are ~66.3%. The summary calls FOLK "a small, illiquid name", but ADTV is Rp6.2bn with zero zero-volume days in three months, above the Rp2bn house floor [S0]; section 5 itself calls it "adequate for a small position". Section 3 also has a "-22.4% per cent" typo.
challenges.answer: The register figures are now flagged as dated 4 November but reflecting the register before the 3 November block, with the direction of the adjustment stated (free float nearer a third, insider block lower). "Illiquid" is removed from the summary and the text describes a small-cap with thin depth relative to market capitalisation. The "-22.4% per cent" typo is not present in the current text, but the per-cent phrasing was re-read and renders as a single value from the F6 fact.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull (Rp25.8) is only the 20% discount: its revenue +3pp shock is inert in the asset SOTP, Traya stays at Rp0.25bn despite a sourced ~Rp5.5bn annualised incremental revenue run-rate [S19], and the Rp18.4bn Q3 gain that could lift the residual or Traya is not booked. The reverse DCF quantifies a market Traya option but no value is carried.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear (Rp19.3) only widens the discount to 40%; the Rp64.74bn residual (55% of NAV, 70% of gross parts) is held at full book although the report calls it an upper bound for a -Rp9.6bn EBITDA estate, and a 50%/100% write-down gives ~Rp16.4/Rp10.2. DGNS (30% of gross parts) is never stressed; a 30%/50% fall gives ~Rp21.0/Rp19.9. There is no capital-deployment or dilution bear.

assumption_realism.note: The operating path is realistic: Q2 SG&A is 95.7% of revenue (5.037/5.262), gross margin 51.5% vs 52% modelled, and FY2026 revenue annualises near Rp19bn; 100% opex is a rounded-up hold. The marks are not: the residual is a plug, Traya is at related-party cost, the discount is applied to net cash, and the overhead is 10% of consolidated SG&A. FY2026E np_parent -Rp6.65 contradicts 9M +Rp18.40, and D&A 18% undercuts FY2025's 21%.

evidence_and_citations.note: Core facts verify (S2, S3, S5, S6/S7, S11, S16, S19/S20, S33, S4/S28, S17, S18, S10). Failures: the S33 RSS snippet is used as a cause of the price fall and as a signal about the holder's view although it has no date/price; the 31 Mar 2027 audit-date catalyst cites S19, which has no date; post_bs_review asserts "no asset sale" without a filing; the holdco_discount basis cites "HSC exclusion" contradicted by S17; free float/insider percentages are pre-3 November.

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP is parent book plus a DGNS mark-up: 64.74 + 0.25 + 27.46 + 25.36 = 117.81. DGNS at market is correct and the parent-equity treatment of minorities is correct, but the largest part is a residual not a mark, the 30% discount is applied to Rp25.36bn of net cash (~+Rp1.9/share if excluded), Traya is at cost, and the holdco card's look-through earnings, dividend-upstream coverage and factor tags are absent. COE 11.85%/WACC are the house build; 30% matches the peer mode.

bias_and_tone.note: The SELL survives doubling the bear probability (weighted TP ~Rp21.7), so it is not one-input-heroic. But the prose overreaches: "illiquid" on Rp6.2bn ADTV, the whole market-cap gap attributed to Traya though 55% of NAV is a residual, "no asset sale" asserted without a filing, and "HSC exclusion" contradicted by section 2. The rating is evidence-led; the target is one-sidedly cautious.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity, royalty or realisation basis applies. The report reads the macro deck's 5.29% FY2027 real GDP correctly, the 30% holdco discount matches the CONGLOMERATES peer mode (ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/DSSA 30%; TOBA/BHIT 40%; ASII 25%), and COE 11.85% is the house build. The USD/IDR 18,350 path is not wired into a rupiah-cost model, which is acceptable but could be stated.

conservatism_audit.note: Two-sided. Conservative: Traya at Rp0.25bn vs ~Rp5.5bn run-rate revenue; the Q3 +Rp18.4bn attributable uplift is not carried; the 30% discount is applied to net cash; FY2027 growth 5% is below GDP 5.29%. Optimistic: the residual is at full book for a -Rp9.6bn EBITDA estate; the holdco overhead deduction is only Rp20bn (10% of consolidated SG&A; a DSSA-like Rp38.8bn carry cuts the target to ~Rp19.0); the bear holds book; D&A 18% vs FY2025's 21%. The revenue-growth shocks are inert, so the mirrored test is nominal.

calibration.note: qc passes and all three BLOCK/WARN flags are justified. The +21.3pp EBITDA-margin move is the 125% FY2025 SG&A ratio against the 95.7% Q2 run-rate, sourced to S0. But FY2026E np_parent -Rp6.65 against 9M actual +Rp18.40 implies a -Rp25.05bn Q4 with no source, and the D&A ratio is moved from 21% to 18% without a sourced reason. The forecast balance sheet is an operating roll excluded from valuation, which is acceptable, but the P&L is presented as as-reported.

signoff.notes: APPROVED at sign-off (update v3). QC verdict PASS, bias neutral (judge 0.96). All red-team challenges are answered (C1-C8 MATERIAL and C9-C11 MINOR accepted and fixed). Lint PASS. Valuation: SOTP Rp24, target Rp27 (-54.1%), SELL; a 30% mid-range holdco discount on a net-cash holding, with related-party, no-dividend and disclosure flags offset by net cash; the discount-on-cash convention is disclosed with the ~1/7 cross-check. The Q3 non-cash asset step-up is carried in the bridge at face value with the evidence gap stated; the release's profit is below-EBIT and non-cash and is correctly not treated as a turnaround. FOLK is not konglo/HSC, so there is no group-consistency issue. QC FIX items Q1-Q2: not blocking - text only, no target or rating effect. findings.finding: The size of the recent price fall is mis-stated as "a fall of about an eighth" [S0] (Investment summary). The S0 monthly series has the October close at Rp64.0 and the 4 November close at Rp59.0, which is -7.8% (about a thirteenth); the last level quoted with a source is Rp77 in [S2], from which Rp59 is -23.4% (about a quarter, and consistent with the ~-24% move under review). "About an eighth" matches neither. The causation wording is correct: the report explicitly calls the S33 sale a post-hoc supply disclosure, "not a proven cause of the fall", and section 5 repeats that it is not a signal about the holder's view.

The C11 typo persists in a different form. Section 3 renders "operating expenses fell -22.4% per cent in 2025": F6 carries unit "pct" and the template appends "per cent", so the text has both a double unit ("% per cent") and a double negative ("fell -22.4%", i.e. a rise). The C11 response says the typo "is not present in the current text", which is contradicted by the rendered report.

The bridge item F23 (Rp18.40bn) is np_parent_9m for the nine months, but fund record labels it "Q3-2026 attributable profit" and section 4 calls it the Q3 step-up carried "at the Rp18.40bn attributable amount reported for the nine months". The June-anchored residual already contains H1; the Q3-only attributable profit is about Rp21.15bn (9M Rp18.40bn less H1 parent -Rp2.75bn from S0 Q1/Q2 np_parent of +15.23 and -17.98), so the bridge understates NAV by ~Rp2.75bn (~1.9%). The amount is sourced and the treatment is conservative, not aggressive.

Section 5's memo stress fractions do not match the arithmetic. Halving the residual removes Rp32.37bn of Rp141.46bn NAV, i.e. 22.9% (not "about three tenths"); a full write-down removes 45.8% (not "about three fifths"); and the resulting target of ~Rp12.6 is ~21% of the Rp59 price (about a fifth, not "roughly a sixth"). The target levels themselves (high teens; ~Rp13) are right.

The frontmatter summary ("FOLK trades at Rp59 after anchor supply and a weak tape") and thesis bullet 5 ("the anchor holder is still selling [S2][S33][S10]") retain a temporal/causal lean toward the S33 snippet that the body correctly disclaims. S33 carries no transaction date or price, so "still selling" asserts continuation the archive cannot support; S2 evidences only the October block.
